heading: Application for Associate Consultant, Digital Forensics and Incident Response
paragraphs: I am applying for the Associate Consultant role in Digital Forensics and Incident Response in London. The work described, preserving digital data to an evidential standard and then explaining what the evidence shows, is the part of security I have been working towards since my Master's. Control Risks interests me because the practice spans law firms, multinationals and law enforcement clients, which means the investigations are varied and the standard of evidence is high. I would rather start my career somewhere that treats documentation as part of the technical work rather than an administrative task.

My day-to-day work already runs on the same discipline. In my IT support role I investigate four or five suspicious emails a day, check sender and link domains for impersonation, document what I find and warn colleagues about recurring tactics. For my Master's I designed a phishing analysis prototype that mapped suspicious email indicators to MITRE ATT&CK techniques and then evaluated it against a mixture of suspicious and legitimate business emails. The point of that testing was to find where the tool was wrong. That habit, treating false positives as the central problem rather than an afterthought, is what I would bring to forensic analysis, where a weak finding in a report has consequences beyond the case.

On the systems side, I support around fifteen users across fifteen to twenty devices, working with Windows, Microsoft 365 and Azure, and I run the access request process through on-premises Active Directory. I use Python and PowerShell for scripting and log analysis, and I built a local tool that maps Windows error codes to likely causes so recurring faults can be investigated from a known starting point. My Master's modules included digital forensics and network security, and my cryptography and critical infrastructure modules covered evidence handling at a conceptual level. For a DFIR team, the gain is a graduate who can image and examine an endpoint, script the repetitive parts and write up what was found in language a non-technical reader can follow.

I want to be straightforward about where I would be starting. I have not worked on live forensic acquisitions or produced expert reports, and my knowledge of the standards you cite is from academic study rather than casework. What I do bring is the analytical method those standards exist to protect, and I am willing to put in the work to reach an evidential standard under supervision.
I would welcome the chance to discuss the role further. My CV is attached, and I am happy to answer any questions about my experience or my projects.
